title: Two LLM adapters as a design-verification twin
summary: Two model adapters built on different internals are shipped against the one streaming vocabulary from the start, so that anything the vocabulary cannot express for both is treated as a vocabulary bug.
firstReason: The Go design should keep proving the provider-neutral stream contract with two independent adapters; the second one cannot be the npm pi-ai library, so the LLM area must name a Go counterpart.

title: Bounded recovery for transient LLM request failures
summary: A failed model request carries one serializable failure record (message, code, status, retry-after, request id) with no policy in it. A listener on the request-error extension point decides whether to retry, within fixed bounds.
firstReason: Separating failure facts from retry policy keeps adapters simple and recovery bounded; the Go design should keep the same split.

title: Provider-routed LLM adapters and a generic pi-ai backend
summary: Model adapters are registered by provider name, and every request carries a provider and a model; one provider has exactly one adapter owner. A generic adapter can serve many providers.
firstReason: Separating which provider owns a request from which model it runs is needed for gateways and for switching models inside a session; keep it, with a Go counterpart for the generic pi-ai backend.

title: Create every message as an identified immutable value
summary: Every message (user, assistant or tool result) gets an opaque id when it is created and keeps it through the inbox, the durable log and the model request. A message is immutable after creation.
firstReason: One identity per message through every representation removes correlation guesswork; Go keeps the rule and enforces immutability by not exposing mutable fields.

title: Projected token usage and context occupancy
summary: Token totals and context occupancy are durable session projections folded from the whole log, so they survive paging and compaction and include failed attempts. The browser no longer derives them from the conversation nodes it happens to have loaded.
firstReason: Billing and context-pressure numbers must come from the full log, not from a window of the UI; keep the projections.

title: Terminal LLM stream failures
summary: The LLM runtime is the one place that turns an adapter failure into a terminal finish record (error or aborted). Errors from middleware, consumers or message assembly stay thrown as defects and never enter request recovery.
firstReason: One normalization boundary gives the loop a single failure shape to handle; in Go the adapter returns an error or a terminal chunk and the runtime normalizes both.

title: DeepSeek LLM API request extensions for session logs and plugin packages
summary: A registry lets plugins add extra top-level fields to requests sent to the official DeepSeek API; it is used to upload the session log and the list of plugin packages. Extensions are best effort and never fail the model request.
firstReason: It is a product feature of the official DeepSeek adapter and should be kept; the package-list field must be redefined for compiled-in components and plugin processes.

title: Producer-owned message sources at the V4 edge
summary: A message's source kind names its producer directly (for example system-prompt or compact-basic) instead of a generic plugin wrapper; the V3 to V4 migration converts old wrappers with a fixed table.
firstReason: Producer-owned source kinds are kept as the native shape of the Go format; the V3 to V4 conversion table is not needed because upstream files are not read.

title: Account provider and active request cancellation
summary: The API-key route and the account route are separate provider routes, each with exactly one credential source and no fallback to the other. Signing out cancels every running agent whose latest logged request used the account route, keeping their inboxes.
firstReason: Falling back between credentials would silently change who is billed. Reading the route from the request already logged in the session avoids a second 'current provider' field that can drift.

title: DeepSeek account models come from the account listing and gate by client version
summary: On the account route the model list comes from the account service, loaded lazily per credential, refreshed in the background and falling back to the last good list or the built-in catalog. A listed model is offered only if its declared minimum client version is met; unknown models without that declaration stay hidden.
firstReason: New models reach users without a release, and an old build cannot request a model it cannot drive. Inference: the Go client needs its own identity and version in that gate, which is a question for the provider area.

title: Context breakdown retains only system prompts
summary: The context-breakdown projection keeps only the surviving system prompts and one running total, instead of one entry per message. Its saved state no longer grows with conversation length.
firstReason: Per-message entries made the projection cache megabytes large and slow to validate on every session listing. Bounded projection state is a rule for every Go projection.

title: Pi-ai system reminder fallback
summary: For models without native mid-conversation system messages, the multi-provider adapter turns each later system message into a user message wrapped in `<system-reminder>` before sending. Stored messages keep their original roles.
firstReason: Folding later system messages into the first prompt invalidates the provider's cached prefix on every update. The trigger is the behaviour of the pi-ai library, but the rule (the adapter adapts, the log stays truthful) applies to whatever Go adapter serves models without that capability.

title: The official DeepSeek route follows the official model listing until its catalog is customized
summary: The API-key route follows the official model listing only while it talks to the official endpoint and the user has not customised the model catalog. A customised catalog wins whole and stops listing requests.
firstReason: New official models reach API-key users without a release, while a user's edited catalog, or a gateway behind a custom base URL, is never overridden. This is product behaviour of the provider.

title: Producer-declared context forms
summary: A non-user message's source may declare a `form`, a small semantic vocabulary for the shape of the information (for example `instructions` read from workspace files, or a `catalog` of available items), separate from `kind`, which says who produced it. The UI chooses presentation from the form; colours and layout never enter the vocabulary.
firstReason: It replaces a raw JSON dump with a readable row while keeping presentation out of the log. A semantic tag on the event is easy for a host template to switch on.

title: DeepSeek through the Anthropic Messages protocol
summary: The DeepSeek adapter speaks the Anthropic Messages protocol under one `deepseek-official` route, keeping thinking blocks, signatures, tool calls and cumulative usage as protocol fields instead of flattening them. A prepared call freezes endpoint, credential reference and model capabilities, so retries stay on one configuration.
firstReason: Flattening assistant history loses information that later tool turns need. The protocol mapping is provider behaviour and has to be implemented faithfully again in Go.

title: Model selector badges come from the model listing
summary: A model's badge in the selector (text and tone) comes from the service's `/models` listing, under the `deepseek-harness` key of `client_metadata`, not from a client package that matches model names. The text is limited to 1 to 12 visible characters on one line, and control characters are rejected.
firstReason: Changing a release marker should not need a client release, and the listing is an external service contract that the Go adapter reads the same way. Validation of the text happens on the host.

title: Expose DeepSeek deferred-only request failures
summary: When every tool in a DeepSeek request is declared as deferred, the adapter sends the request unchanged and reports the provider's rejection. It no longer inserts a placeholder tool to make the request acceptable.
firstReason: A placeholder hid invalid tool-update state, changed the cached request prefix and advertised a tool nothing could execute. Surfacing the provider error is the honest behaviour in any language.

title: Prune unused stream visibility helpers
summary: Proposal: remove five exported helper functions that classify whether a streamed chunk is visible, because no product code calls them.
firstReason: Adopt by omission: the Go model package should contain the first-token reader that session statistics and the trajectory view use, and not these five queries.

title: Use node:timers/promises for hand-rolled cancellable sleeps
summary: Rejected proposal: replace three hand-written cancellable sleeps with Node's built-in promise timers. Rejected because the test framework's fake clock does not intercept the built-in, so tests would become slow or non-deterministic.
firstReason: Exists only because of Node and Vitest: both the proposal and its rejection are about a Node built-in and a JavaScript test clock. A cancellable wait in Go is a `select` on a timer and the context.
